body:
> it turns out that I was getting the message because `start()` was being called while the timer's parent was being deleted

You might want to use `is_queued_for_deletion()` to check whether you can start the timer like this:

```gdscript
func _on_body_exited(_body: Node2D) -> void:
	if not is_queued_for_deletion():
		_timer.start()
```

@Rubonnek Thanks for the suggestion, but my point with this issue isn't that I can't make it work. I most definitely can - there's `is_inside_tree()`, there's the ordering that I mentioned in the issue, there's `is_queued_for_deletion()` that you suggested, I could also disconnect the signal before `queue_free()` etc. All of which are fairly simple to do.
My point was that I think the code that reproduces the issue is fairly normal and common and (to my knowledge) isn't breaking any of the documented rules, but it is still producing an error with quite misleading message for this specific situation. I just thought that should be improved.

> My point was that I think the code that reproduces the issue is fairly normal and common and (to my knowledge) isn't breaking any of the documented rules

Well, the code you've presented and the fact that to you this type of code logic is fairly normal and common and should be handled by the engine does seem to point out you are assuming Godot has (or should have) a built-in garbage collection for this type of situation and Godot clearly does not. Unlike Unity, and other engines with garbage collection, Godot won't automatically clean up certain scenarios that in those engines are fairly common. In Godot, it's up to the user to provide the cleaning logic for these situations, and this is due to performance reasons -- the garbage collector could stutter the engine at an inconvenient time and therefore cause inconsistent performance and that's why there's no garbage collector in Godot.

> but it is still producing an error with quite misleading message for this specific situation. I just thought that should be improved.

I agree the message is quite confusing in this scenario.

I think the best possible solution here would be to modify the error message to be more generic, such as the following:

```
Unable to start the timer since it is not inside the scene tree.
```
Given that is exactly what the error is checking for:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/19bb18716ef08b811fec330cba4d35fbdb027bcc/scene/main/timer.cpp#L116-L117

@Rubonnek 

> Well, the code you've presented and the fact that to you this type of code logic is fairly normal and common and should be handled by the engine does seem to point out you are assuming Godot has (or should have) a built-in garbage collection for this type of situation and Godot clearly does not.

I'm aware that Godot does not have garbage collection (which is actually one of the things I like about it). Also, I'm not sure why you came to such a conclusion. Are there any leaks in the project that I'm not aware of?
The reason I described the scenario as "normal" is because it's not breaking any rules or guidelines described by the documentation. The `Timer` was added to the tree. And `queue_free()` was called instead of `free()` to allow everything to finish that needs finishing before the node is deleted. If you're aware of a rule or piece of documentation that the code is breaking, I'd appreciate it if you told me.

I didn't immediately come to a conclusion that the best solution is to change the message because I don't know Godot's source code enough to know that other solutions are not viable. But based on what I've seen while debugging, I did expect that that will be the case. And if that really is the case, then I agree with you that generalizing the message would be better, although the previous message did advise using `autostart` which I think might be lost in a generalized message.

> I'm aware that Godot does not have garbage collection (which is actually one of the things I like about it). Also, I'm not sure why you came to such a conclusion.

Aside from what I've already stated, it seemed to me you thought Godot has a garbage collection because you wrote this:

> * I think I'd be happy with any other solution that either makes that code work without an error (this would be preferred)

And also this:

> I'm not sure what the fix should be, but I have a few ideas that seem sensible to me:
>
> * The `body_exited` signal never gets triggered when the `Area2D` is leaving the tree.

which seems to imply you want the timer start error handled entirely by the engine. Which in turn made me think of how a `GameObject` in Unity can be disabled rather easily in comparison to Godot -- if I recall Unity also turns of the signals the object might emit when disabling them. I'm not too familiar with Unity, I've only heard of other developers disliking how different disabling nodes are in Godot, but I suppose attempting to free the object in Unity will either disable the signals of the object or trigger the garbage collection to also disable the signals, which in turn brought me to garbage collection. You are attempting to `queue_free()` the `BuggyScene` directly here.

> And `queue_free()` was called instead of `free()` to allow everything to finish that needs finishing before the node is deleted.

The documentation never specifies that everything is allowed to finish. The engine waits for the node's deferred calls to finish if any [as stated in the Node.queue_free() documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html#class-node-method-queue-free) -- that's it. The engine does not wait for the signal callbacks (i.e. `body_exited` signal in this case) to be handled properly by the associated callables, which is the case you are presenting here.

> although the previous message did advise using `autostart` which I think might be lost in a generalized message.

Thanks for bringing this up. I did keep the autostart advice in the message when I submitted the pull request.

@Rubonnek First things first - the message. I think the "Either add it or set autostart to true" part still implies that the problem is that it was never added, which is what was misleading in the first place. I gave it some thought and I'd suggest that the message be:
"Unable to start the timer because it's not inside the scene tree. If you are trying to start it before adding it to the scene tree, you might want to use autostart.". Or something in similar fashion.
That way, there's no assumption that the only cause of the error is the `Timer` never being added to the scene tree.

As for the rest... What I had in mind when I wrote this:

> I think I'd be happy with any other solution that either makes that code work without an error (this would be preferred)

was something like doing the signaling caused by `Area2D`' being removed from the scene in a different "phase" from actually removing nodes from the scene tree. Something like a "pre-exit-tree" phase. But I didn't find anything like that, so I was just hoping I missed something. I have no experience with Unity, but thanks for the explanation - your conclusion makes a bit more sense to me now.
Another suggestion I had was `Area2D` not signalling about bodies leaving when the event is *caused by `Area2D` being deleted*. This I think is easily doable, but I also assumed there was a reason it was made that way that I'm missing. I didn't mean to imply that the engine should do any magic for me.

As for `queue_free()`, I didn't think it was doing anything else than what you wrote, but since it's moving the deletion to the end of the frame, that should mean that at the point of deletion:
- `_process()` is done (and signals triggered during it)
- `_physics_process()` is done (and it's signals)
- all differed calls
Since I wasn't doing anything else, I expected the code to work without issues. I mean, the signal is emitted by `Area2D` *as it's being deleted*. It's not caused by my code and because of that, it wasn't something I expected.

I still think this is on Godot and it shouldn't happen, but we can agree to disagree. And I've learned to add my timers as children before everything else 😄

> First things first - the message. I think the "Either add it or set autostart to true" part still implies that the problem is that it was never added, which is what was misleading in the first place. I gave it some thought and I'd suggest that the message be:
> "Unable to start the timer because it's not inside the scene tree. If you are trying to start it before adding it to the scene tree, you might want to use autostart.". Or something in similar fashion.

I find the new message confusing due to the use of the word "before". I don't have the last word on what gets merged or doesn't. I encourage you to submit a pull request.

> Another suggestion I had was `Area2D` not signalling about bodies leaving when the event is _caused by `Area2D` being deleted_. 

The change you've proposed is easily doable, and to avoid breaking backwards compatibility that would require adding a boolean to the class just for this feature. However the same goes for the workarounds you've already found, and other workarounds such as writing your own custom `queue_free()` wrapper that disconnects all, or some, of the signals of the node before actually calling `queue_free()`.

Again, feel free to submit a PR for this change if you wish, however I don't think it will be accepted for Godot 4.x because it adds unnecessary complexity, but again I don't have the last word on what gets merged. It might get merged for a later version.
